_proxy_ip_doc: Public edge = oci-analytics (129.151.228.66). gcp-proxy:443 is closed publicly (session goal: gcp-proxy is wg-only). Public clients hit oci-analytics:443 which runs caddy-public — a layer4 SNI mux: mail (imap./smtps.) → maddy L4; pure-public SNIs (gh-pages + auth=none) → local :8443 L7 serve; everything else → raw-TLS passthrough to gcp-proxy 10.1.0.2:443 over wg-public, where TLS terminates + path-routes + the @wg gate runs. WG0 clients (hickory at 10.0.0.1:53) resolve via the multi-value extra_ip directly to gcp-proxy 10.0.0.1.
_proxy_ip6_doc: IPv6 twin of proxy_ip: oci-analytics VNIC address, declared in c_vps/vps_oci (oci_core_ipv6.analytics_v6, output analytics_ipv6). Every a_record WITHOUT a per-record ip override gets an AAAA to this (or to its own ip6). Without it an IPv6-only uplink (no NAT64/DNS64) cannot reach the fleet at all (#519). Requires ::/0 tcp/443 in the OCI security list.

dns_records._a_records_doc: SPLIT-HORIZON: PUBLIC Cloudflare wildcard '*' resolves to proxy_ip (public edge) ONLY — NO RFC1918 mesh IPs in public DNS (avoids topology leak + blackholing public clients that pick an unroutable internal IP). Internal wg0 mesh resolution is handled by Hickory (10.0.0.1:53, separate engine) which returns the mesh IP for wg clients. PER-RECORD OVERRIDES: 'ip' field on any record overrides the global proxy_ip for that single name. 'extra_ips' (if ever needed) adds public-routable IPs only to the multi-value set; the engine emits one cloudflare_record per (name, ip). NEVER put mesh/RFC1918 IPs in extra_ips — they belong in Hickory, not public CF.

a_records.comment: Wildcard → oci-analytics (public edge) ONLY. Internal wg0 mesh resolution is split-horizon via Hickory (10.0.0.1:53), NOT a public CF record — keeps RFC1918 mesh IPs off public DNS.

a_records.name: api
a_records.comment: api.* → public edge (oci-analytics). Public /pub/* routes here; internal wg-cloud routes resolve via Hickory split-horizon, not a public mesh record.

adopted._doc: Live objects that existed before (or outside) this code and are ADOPTED by import blocks in zero-trust-adopted.tf, so the live account and the repo agree (#994). Values mirror the live account: a non-empty plan diff on any of them means the code is wrong, never the account.

vnet.name: default
vnet.comment: This network was autogenerated because this account lacked a default one

smtp_tunnel.name: smtp-proxy-tunnel
smtp_tunnel._doc: Down, 0 connectors (dead ingress, clean-up candidate). Adopted as-is; its secret is not readable, so secret is ignored.

zero_trust._doc: Cloudflare One (Zero Trust) — PRIMARY auth + network edge, Authelia stays the FALLBACK. Design: a0_docs/eng-specs/cloudflare-zero-trust.md. Rendered by zero-trust.tf. Phase 1 = tunnel + cloudflared on oci-apps (always on) + ONE pilot Access app, ONE service token, ONE Gateway private-DNS override (gated by org_enabled). No existing hostname is touched in phase 1.
zero_trust._org_enabled_doc: false until the owner enables Zero Trust on the account (dashboard → Zero Trust → pick team name → Free plan). The 2026-10-14 probe returned access.api.error.not_enabled. While false, ONLY the tunnel (no public hostname, catch-all 404) is created — nothing is exposed. Flip to true, then run the cf-zero-trust workflow [zt:plan] → [zt:apply] → [zt:verify].
zero_trust._tunnel_ingress_doc: false = tunnel fleet-edge keeps only the catch-all 404 (pilot apply is pure creates). true adds the spec-zt ingress rule: one in-place update of cloudflare_zero_trust_tunnel_cloudflared_config.zt_fleet; rollback = set false and re-apply.

tunnel.name: fleet-edge
tunnel._doc: ONE remotely-managed tunnel for the whole fleet. Connectors (cloudflared replicas) run on fleet VMs and reach origins over the WireGuard mesh (10.0.0.0/24), so a hostname can point at any VM. Phase 1: one replica on oci-apps (a_solutions/infra-net_cloudflared). Credentials: tunnel token in sops only.

identity._doc: No IdP existed (Access was never enabled). Phase 1 = Cloudflare one-time PIN (no client secret to manage, mail to me@ arrives via CF Email Routing → worker → Gmail + Stalwart). Phase 2 adds Google (OAuth client the owner creates) as the primary button; OTP stays as break-glass.

pilot_app._doc: Pilot = cloud-spec (static spec site, busybox httpd on oci-apps :3080, read-only, no user data). Its EXISTING route https://cloud.diegonmarcos.com/spec/ (Caddy + Authelia + WG gate) is untouched; the pilot adds a NEW hostname next to it. The DNS record depends_on the Access app, so the hostname is never live without Access in front.
pilot_app.name: cloud-spec (zt pilot)

service_tokens.name: zt-pilot-machine
service_tokens._doc: Machine bearer for API/MCP/CI clients: send CF-Access-Client-Id + CF-Access-Client-Secret headers. Secret leaves terraform only sops-encrypted (src/secrets.zt-service-token.yaml).

private_dns._doc: Gateway DNS location 'fleet' + DNS override policies = private names resolved by Cloudflare. Names live under fleet.internal (ICANN-reserved .internal: never collides with the public zone or its '*' wildcard, and never leaks to public DNS). Hickory (10.0.0.1) stays the fleet resolver and fallback; phase 2 points Hickory's forwarder at this location (DoT/DoH).
